newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: PALM OIL - Asian markets seen in Christmas drift.
newsitem.headline: PALM OIL - Asian markets seen in Christmas drift.

text.p: Southeast Asian palm oil markets are likely to be range-bound during the shortened year-end holiday week, regional traders said.
"It's going to be a holiday market. I'll be surprised if it trades at all," a Singapore trader at a U.S. commodity company said.

Another Singapore dealer for a European trading house said the March futures contract on the Kuala Lumpur Commodities Exchange would probably range between 1,200-1,250 ringgit ($476.19-$496.03) a tonne this week.
The March futures contract closed on Friday at 1,230 ringgit.
"The whole market will just be very quiet," the Singapore dealer said.
Palm oil prices might, at most, inch up on the back of export data due this week, but any gains would be capped by the holiday lethargy, dealers said.

The market expects cargo surveyor Societe Generale de Surveillance (SGS) Malaysia Sdn Bhd to announce the December 1-25 palm oil export data this week. Dealers say the figures are likely to be bullish.
"Apart from the export data, we don't expect much activity as most people will be in the Christmas and New Year mood," a Kuala Lumpur trader said.
In Indonesia, another trader said the margin between crude palm oil and palm olein was slim and that palm olein had to adjust higher to be profitable to refiners.
"I think olein prices will rise, but not by too much because BULOG has already set the ceiling at 1,500 rupiah," the trader said.
Beddu Amang, the head of the state logistics agency BULOG, has said olein prices should not exceed 1,500 rupiah/kg before the Moslem Ramadan fasting month, which begins in January.
Indonesian palm olein finished last week at 1,445-50 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, compared with 1,425-30 a week ago.
(With contributions from K.T. Arasu from Jakarta and Rene Pastor from Singapore)
